about: E9 registry: the single place a source or layer is declared. `groups` are the two origins (crc-sdk adapters, new in crc-lab); `sources` is what the page lists, each with an `origin` (one entry per data source, in display order); every layer names its `source_id`. kinds: h3-cells (file per horizon), tracks (IBTrACS storm records), points-binary (packed point records with an index.json), points / lines (GeoJSON), geojson (static outline).

sources.title: Tropical cyclone tracks
sources.provider: NOAA NCEI IBTrACS v04r01 (North Atlantic basin), read through crc-sdk's IBTrACSPlan
sources.short: Best-track positions and winds of every storm that crossed Texas since 1950.
sources.returns: Track points every six hours: position, agency wind (knots), pressure, Saffir-Simpson category.
sources.coverage: North Atlantic basin; here, storms with a point inside the Texas box, 1950–2025.
sources.licence: U.S. government work; attribution requested (Schreck et al. 2024, doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16)
caveats: Observations, not a hazard model: a track point is where the centre was, not the wind at any place.
Agency winds differ in averaging period (WMO 10-minute, US 1-minute) and are missing for older storms; the wind_source field says which was used.
Tracks are clipped to a Gulf box, so Atlantic origins are cut off.

sources.title: Coastal water levels
sources.provider: NOAA CO-OPS Extreme Water Levels, read through crc-sdk's NOAAExtremeWaterLevelPlan
sources.short: Published annual-exceedance water levels at Texas tide stations.
sources.returns: Per station, 22 published levels (1.01 to 100 years) relative to the station datum, plus the sea-level trend.
sources.coverage: The 9 of 39 Texas water-level stations that publish the product.
sources.licence: U.S. government work; attribution requested (NOAA CO-OPS)

sources.title: Airport station temperatures
sources.provider: NOAA GHCNh hourly observations, curves fitted by crc-sdk (GEV, L-moments)
sources.short: Hottest hour of the year at airport stations, 2000–2024, as a fitted curve per station.
sources.returns: Per station, a return-level curve of the annual maximum hourly temperature.
sources.coverage: Texas airport (USW) stations with at least 15 valid years in 2000–2024; 8 so far.
sources.licence: CC0-1.0 per the AWS registry; attribution requested (NOAA GHCNh)

sources.title: ERA5 reanalysis baseline
sources.provider: ECMWF ERA5 (1.5° WeatherBench2 copy), curves fitted by crc-sdk (GEV, L-moments)
sources.short: Hottest day of the year, 1991–2020, as a fitted curve per H3 resolution-4 cell.
sources.returns: Cells with return levels of the annual maximum daily temperature from a historical reanalysis.
sources.coverage: Texas and surroundings, 1,439 land cells of about 1,770 km².
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0; contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information

sources.title: CRC Open climate projections
sources.provider: RiskThinking.AI CMIP6-based projections (CRC Open release), read through crc-sdk
sources.short: Pre-fitted curves of 63 climate indices on H3 cells under one high-emissions pathway (SSP5-8.5).
sources.returns: Per cell and horizon, a return-level curve per hazard; eight hazards loaded, all 63 listed.
sources.coverage: Global release; here, cells intersecting Texas, horizons 2030, 2050 and 2080.
caveats: High-emissions case (SSP5-8.5), not a forecast. One pathway, pooled model ensemble, no historical baseline in the release.
Regional screening: a value is the curve for a whole cell (about 253 km² at resolution 5), not any site in it.

sources.title: Storm reports
sources.provider: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, cleaned by crc-lab (Phase 2)
sources.short: Hail, wind, tornado, flood and other reports from the National Weather Service, 1950 to date.
sources.returns: One record per report: type, time (UTC), magnitude (hail inches, wind knots), damage, location or county/zone.
sources.coverage: Texas, 1950–2026 (tornado only before 1955; hail and wind from 1955; all types from 1996).

sources.title: Hail and gust curves from storm reports
sources.provider: crc-lab curves fitted from NOAA Storm Events reports (Phase 3), brought into CRC with crc-sdk from_table
sources.short: Largest hail and strongest thunderstorm wind of the year, 1996–2025, as a curve per H3 cell.
sources.returns: Per resolution-5 cell, a return-level curve of the annual maximum hail size and thunderstorm gust.
sources.coverage: Texas cells, reports 1996–2025; horizon 2025 is the end of the observed window.
sources.licence: Derived from U.S. government data; attribution to NOAA NCEI
caveats: Built from storm reports, not measurements: reports follow people and roads, so an empty or low cell may be unobserved rather than calm.
Regional screening: a value is the curve for a whole cell (about 253 km²).

sources.title: Solar plants with value and hail exposure
sources.provider: USGS / Berkeley Lab solar database (USPVDB v4.0), valued with NREL ATB cost, hail from NOAA Storm Events reports
sources.short: Texas utility-scale solar plants: capacity, replacement value, and hail reports around each plant.
sources.returns: Per plant: capacity, a benchmark replacement value, the local hail report rate and sizes, and hail and gust return levels from the cell curves.
sources.coverage: Texas plants of 1 MW or more in the April 2026 database release; hail reports 1996–2025.
sources.licence: U.S. government works (USGS, NOAA) and NREL ATB; attribution requested
caveats: Hail numbers come from storm reports, which follow people and roads. The circle around a plant grows until it holds 100 reports, never smaller than 10 km.
The annual chance of hail at the plant rests on a placeholder: the area hit per report (25 km²) has no source.
Value is a national benchmark cost per kW times capacity, not the plant's own cost or insured value.

sources.title: Hail days: sources compared
sources.provider: NOAA NCEI Storm Events reports; NOAA MRMS radar hail size (MESH); NOAA NCEI Severe Weather Data Inventory radar hail signatures; reporting-bias model from crc-lab
sources.short: Four records of hail days per year for the same cells, side by side, by swipe or as a ratio.
sources.returns: Per H3 resolution-5 cell, hail days per year from storm reports (1 inch or more, 1996–2025), the same corrected for reporting bias, radar hail size of 30 mm or more (MRMS, 2020–2025) and radar hail signatures of 1.25 inches or more (NEXRAD, 1995–2025).
sources.coverage: 2,566 Texas cells. The four records cover different years and measure different things.
sources.licence: U.S. government works (NOAA NCEI, NOAA MRMS open data); attribution requested
caveats: Storm reports need a person nearby: empty country looks calm. The corrected record divides by a fitted reporting rate from population and roads; it is a model, not an observation.
Radar hail size (MRMS MESH) sees everywhere but over-calls: it is built to exceed most observed stones, and five years is a short record.
Radar hail signatures come from single radars, scan by scan; their coverage and algorithm changed over the years, and early years carry missing values.
A hail day is counted per cell of about 253 km², so every record is a regional figure, not a point value.

layers.licence: U.S. government work; attribution requested (Schreck et al. 2024, doi:10.25921/82ty-9e16)

layers.title: Storm Events (NOAA reports)
layers.source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, cleaned by crc-lab

layers.title: Largest hail of the year (reports, 1996–2025)
layers.source: crc-lab curves from NOAA Storm Events reports
layers.licence: Derived from U.S. government data; attribution to NOAA NCEI
layers.caveat: Built from storm reports, not measurements: an empty cell may be unobserved. Annual maxima per cell, pooled with the six neighbouring cells, Gumbel with a zero atom (see data/curves/hail_size.card.json).

layers.title: Strongest thunderstorm wind of the year (reports, 1996–2025)
layers.source: crc-lab curves from NOAA Storm Events reports
layers.licence: Derived from U.S. government data; attribution to NOAA NCEI
layers.caveat: Built from storm reports (mostly estimated gusts), not measurements: an empty cell may be unobserved. Pooled with the six neighbouring cells, Gumbel with a zero atom (see data/curves/thunderstorm_gust.card.json).

layers.title: Coastal water levels, published return levels
layers.source: NOAA CO-OPS Extreme Water Levels, via crc-sdk NOAAExtremeWaterLevelPlan
layers.licence: U.S. government work; attribution requested (NOAA CO-OPS)
layers.caveat: Levels as published by NOAA (annual exceedance probabilities from a detrended series, relative to the station datum); not fitted by crc-sdk. A station is a point, not a stretch of coast.

layers.title: Hottest hour of the year at airport stations, 2000–2024
layers.source: NOAA GHCNh hourly temperature, curves fitted by crc-sdk (GEV, L-moments)
layers.licence: CC0-1.0 per the AWS registry; attribution requested (NOAA GHCNh)
layers.caveat: Historical observations at a point, not a projection; extremes of sampled hourly temperature, not daily TXx. Curves are crc-sdk's fit from 2000–2024 (at least 15 valid years).

layers.title: Hottest day of the year, ERA5 baseline 1991–2020
layers.source: ERA5 reanalysis (1.5° WeatherBench2 copy), curves fitted by crc-sdk (GEV, L-moments)
layers.licence: CC BY 4.0; contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information
layers.caveat: Historical baseline, not a projection: annual maxima 1991–2020 from a 1.5° reanalysis, fitted per H3 resolution-4 cell (about 1,770 km²). Reanalysis underestimates local extremes; a cell is an area average. Horizon 2005 is the window centre.

layers.title: Solar plants (USPVDB), value and local hail
layers.source: USPVDB v4.0; NREL ATB 2025; NOAA Storm Events via crc-lab
layers.licence: U.S. government works and NREL ATB; attribution requested
layers.caveat: Hail figures are report-based and local to a circle around the plant; the annual chance uses a placeholder footprint of 25 km² per report. The curve is the plant's cell curve from Phase 3, a regional value.
